occurrences.source_text: For an explicit check of the archimedean determinant scalar, choose symplectic integral cycles and normalized holomorphic forms `ω1,…,ωg`; write their period matrix `(1,τ)`. Riemann's bilinear identity gives their Gram matrix `Im τ`. The analytic Jacobian is `C^g/(Z^g+τZ^g)` and Abel–Jacobi pulls `dz_i` to `ω_i`. The positive volume of its fundamental parallelepiped is `det Im τ`, so the squared norm of `dz1∧…∧dzg` in the positive top-form convention is exactly `det Im τ`, also the squared determinant norm of the `ω_i`. The top-form integral uses the usual positive ordering of real pairs; changing between block and interleaved complex wedges accounts for the orientation sign, not a positive metric scalar. No `g!`, `π^g`, polarization degree, or isogeny degree occurs. A Kähler form raised to its gth power would require a factorial, but that is not this norm.

occurrences.source_text: dominating Γ. Blowing up a closed regular point of a regular surface is regular: for regular parameters u,v its charts are T[v/u] and T[u/v], and at an exceptional point u and a lift of a uniformizer of the local ring of P1_{κ(x)} form regular parameters. This also covers non-rational closed centres. The resulting Z is integral, proper over R and R-flat (its coordinate rings have no R-torsion); the generic fibre is X, because every centre lies over a finite prime. Indeed Γ→M was already an isomorphism on the entire generic fibre. The two maps are α:Z→M and β:Z→Y, both proper birational, with identity on X.

occurrences.source_text: A continuous pointwise square root b_0 of chi has values in mu_(2m). Equality of cohomology classes means delta(b_0)/epsilon_sign is the coboundary of a continuous sign cochain; correcting b_0 supplies b²=chi and delta b=epsilon_sign. Normalize b(1)=1. On G_L, the cocycle is 1, so b is a character. For h in G_L and g in G_Q, the identities epsilon_sign(g,h)=epsilon_sign(h,g)=1 show b(gh)=b(g)b(h)=b(h)b(g), and then b(ghg^-1)=b(h). Its kernel in G_L is therefore normal in G_Q.

occurrences.source_text: Here is the complete local/global obstruction check. Use the constant-module squaring sequence 1 -> {±1} -> mu_infinity -> mu_infinity -> 1. By local reciprocity, a finite character of G_Qp has a character square root exactly when its character on Qp* does. The torsion factor of Qp* is cyclic of even order; its only obstruction is the value at -1. The valuation Z factor admits a finite-order square root. For odd p, squaring on the pro-p principal units is an automorphism; for p=2 the torsion-free factor 1+4Z_2 is procyclic and its generator's image may be given a square root of twice the order. Thus the criterion holds also at 2, with no omitted principal-unit obstruction. Local H²(G_Qp,{±1}) has two elements, by Kummer and the local Brauer invariant. The boundary of chi equals the sign class at every finite prime. The latter is zero outside T because its class inflates from the unramified local quotient, which has cohomological dimension one. The global Brauer injection and invariant-sum exact sequence determine the real invariant as well. See the final Milne ADT second edition, I.1.3/I.1.6(b,c), and the proof of II.2.1, printed 164, for the reciprocity and Brauer statements.
